scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a maintenance window, routes for 19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8,
and 90.0.0.0/8 became less stable in r1's RIB. r3 reports
losing an OSPF neighbor. Find the affected link.

injection.action: bring down the link toward r9

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r3 link toward r9
Mechanism: r3 is r9's ONLY backbone neighbor (r9's other
  interface is a stub LAN). r9 owns the 19.0.0.0/8 and
  90.0.0.0/8 prefixes. With the link down, the adjacency
  drops and r9 is fully isolated -- its prefixes disappear
  from the backbone RIBs.
Localization: r3 (eth toward r9)
Root cause: backbone link r3<->r9 is down
Fix: bring the link back up

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault lies on r3's eth0 interface, which is the segment-J link connecting r3 to r9. After the maintenance window, r3's eth0 was left in an administratively/operationally down state (kernel flags show only BROADCAST,MULTICAST — no UP or LOWER_UP). The IP address 39.1.1.1/8 is assigned to the interface, and FRR's OSPF configuration correctly includes "network 39.0.0.0/8 area 0", meaning the interface should be an active OSPF participant — but because the kernel interface is down, OSPF cannot bring it up and reports "eth0 is down / OSPF not enabled on this interface."

r9's eth0 (39.1.1.2/8, the other end of segment J) is fully UP and healthy. r9 is the sole origin of the three affected prefixes: 19.0.0.0/8 (loopback subnets), 39.0.0.0/8 (eth0 directly connected), and 90.0.0.0/8 (eth1 directly connected). With the r3–r9 adjacency broken, r9 has no OSPF neighbor and cannot distribute these routes into the topology. r3 therefore cannot flood them to r1, and r1's RIB shows all three as completely absent ("% Network not in table"). The "less stable" symptom is consistent with the adjacency repeatedly timing out and the SPF reconverging as the dead timer expired on r9's side.

Root cause: r3's eth0 was brought down (likely via "ip link set eth0 down") during the maintenance window and never restored, severing the only OSPF path between r9 and the rest of the topology.

Corrective fix: On r3, run "ip link set eth0 up". The OSPF adjacency with r9 will re-form, r9's routes will be re-advertised, and r1's RIB will recover 19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8, and 90.0.0.0/8 within one OSPF convergence cycle.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly pinpoints r3's eth0 as the down interface connecting r3 to r9, correctly identifying the r3<->r9 link as affected.
The report explicitly identifies loss of the three prefixes (19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8, 90.0.0.0/8) from RIBs and ties their absence to the r3–r9 adjacency failure.
Proposes bringing r3's eth0 up (ip link set eth0 up), which will restore the OSPF adjacency and recover the missing routes.

The investigation log contains concrete CLI outputs showing r3's eth0 is DOWN, r9's eth0 is UP, r1 lacks the affected routes, and r9 only lists r3 as its OSPF neighbor; the agent's conclusion that the downed r3 eth0 severs r9 from the backbone follows logically. One minor speculative phrasing (that the interface was administratively brought down) is not directly proven by the captured outputs but does not alter the core diagnosis or fix.
